commits.message:
fix(daemon): the daemon's own start rejects when its turn failed, so the supervisor restarts it (uh4)

Medium review of the uh4 change:
- The host's start awaited a turn that settles as `threw`, never a
  rejection, so a start that failed (a key the host could not read) went
  live without its start. It now rejects with the turn's failure, and the
  supervisor ends and restarts the renderer; a daemon-level test drives
  the real start.
- A start that failed no longer counts as taken over, so a gone renderer's
  holds stand until one does take its start. Its end is its one log line.
- A session's click that came with no context says that no lane follows
  it, and the lane module's header says what happens.
- The session-contexts book keeps its bound when a file holds more.
- The profile adapter takes the renderer's name; the renderer's start has
  no pass-through layer.

fix(daemon): a failed start restarts its renderer, and a heap snapshot the disk refuses fails alone (uh4)

High review of the uh4 change:
- A start carries a key, as the spec's Start does: a host that cannot read
  it fails the start, and a renderer whose start failed is ended and
  restarted after its backoff, so a repaired key recovers with no daemon
  restart.
- The host writes a renderer's heap snapshot through a watched stream: a
  disk refusal fails the snapshot (no file) instead of throwing out of the
  stdout handler, and the write is off the loop. The renderer waits for its
  pipe to drain between chunks.
- The profile's directories are made by an adapter, not by createDaemon;
  the session-contexts file is spelled in paths.
- A drain that throws joins the turn's failure instead of replacing it.
- A document store's absent document reads back as absent.
- The renderer's lint file set is spelled once; the wrapper over the user
  config base is gone.

feat(daemon): a renderer's stored state is handed in at its start and changes only by store effects, under its name's profile (uh4)

The renderer opens no file. Its picks, drafts, settings history, doctor
marks, clicked terminals and post-mortems read come back as `store` writes,
which the host holds in memory and writes behind under the profile the
renderer's name derives. A start hands all of it back, so a restarted or
crashed renderer keeps every pick, draft and undo step. The default name
keeps today's layout; a second name writes only under its own profile.

No stored state names a path: an undo step names its layer by role, and the
config origin and client hints a click needs are the host's own session
contexts, kept across a daemon restart so a click acts before the session's
next request. The adapter's persistence entries are gone.

chore(release): set `package.json` to 1.229.0
